fixes.title: Headless sequencer had no validation: POST /api/sequencer/load forwarded raw sequence JSON to the native executor and the bare start path ran it, so an unset 0h/+0 target slewed an unattended remote rig to nowhere (and a checkpoint of it resumed into the same slew)
fixes.summary: Added apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/sequence_wire_validation.dart: a pre-flight that runs on the NATIVE SequenceDefinition wire JSON (the exact artifact Rust executes), mirroring TargetCoordinatesUnsetRule's semantics including its severity split (a placeholder target nothing enabled consumes stays a warning), plus TargetCoordinatesRule/SlewCoordinatesRule ranges made NaN-safe, plus structural checks (unparseable payload, missing/unresolvable root_node_id, duplicate node ids, dangling child ids). handleSequencerLoad now rejects with a 400 body shape-compatible with SequenceValidationException.toJsonBody() BEFORE calling sequencerLoadJson, so the bad tree never enters the executor and the bare start path has nothing wrong to run. handleSequencerResumeFromCheckpoint now pre-checks the tree the resume will actually execute (the open editor sequence when there is one, else the interrupted run's stored snapshot via latestSnapshotForSequenceName + parseFromMap) with the real core TargetCoordinatesUnsetRule, and refuses. Resume scope is deliberately narrow (pointing rule only, and any failure to read the tree lets the resume proceed) so a mid-night resume is never refused over equipment/disk/dark-library state.
fixes.test: cd apps/desktop && flutter test test/headless_api/sequencer_wire_validation_test.dart test/headless_api/sequencer_handlers_test.dart -> 41/41 pass. dart analyze lib/headless_api + the test: no issues; dart format --set-exit-if-changed clean.
fixes.revert_check: Cut BOTH production call sites (the 2-line `final rejection = _rejectInvalidWireSequence(json); if (rejection != null) return rejection;` in handleSequencerLoad and `final rejection = await _rejectUnpointableCheckpoint(); if (rejection != null) return rejection;` in handleSequencerResumeFromCheckpoint), leaving the validator itself intact. 4 of 8 tests failed: the placeholder-target load, the out-of-range coordinate load, the malformed-tree load, and the checkpoint-resume refusal. Restored -> 8/8 pass.
fixes.caveats: The start-side re-validation I first wrote was removed as unreachable: load is the only door into the native executor for the headless API, so a second gate at start could never fire and would have been dead code. Residual, outside my ownership: core code calling backend.sequencerLoadJson() directly on an FFI (host) backend bypasses the HTTP handler entirely - only sequence_executor's own load (already validated) and guiding_sequencer_controls._loadSequence do this today. Also outside my files: SequenceExecutor.resumeFromCheckpoint() itself still validates nothing, so a desktop-initiated resume is unguarded; only the headless endpoint is.

fixes.title: Continue Session dated yesterday's session as 'Today at 14:57'
fixes.summary: quick_start_dialog.dart _formatDate branched on `now.difference(dt).inDays`, which truncates ELAPSED hours: a session that ended at 14:57 yesterday is 19 h old when the app opens at 10:00 and reported 0 days, so the dialog stamped it 'Today'. It now compares calendar days via DateUtils.dateOnly on both sides. Also carried the time-of-day into the 2-6 day branch (which previously dropped it entirely) and routed anything a week old OR future-dated (a clock jump now yields a negative day count instead of falling into the 'Today' branch) to an explicit yyyy-mm-dd date. Grepped the repo for 'Today at ' / 'Yesterday at ' - this dialog is the only site, so there is no sibling copy of the bug.
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/widgets/quick_start_dialog_honesty_test.dart test/widgets/quick_start_dialog_checkpoint_test.dart -> 7/7 pass. The date test pins lastSessionDate at one second before today's midnight: always the previous calendar day, and always under 24 h ago, which is exactly the window inDays rounds to 0.
fixes.revert_check: Replaced the production line `final days = DateUtils.dateOnly(now).difference(DateUtils.dateOnly(dt)).inDays;` with the original `final days = now.difference(dt).inDays;`. Test 'a session from the previous calendar day is not dated "Today"' failed (rendered 'Today at 23:59'). Restored -> passes.
fixes.caveats: Timestamps still come from DateTime.now() rather than clockProvider, so a user-selected timezone does not affect this dialog (that is blocked item 30, owned elsewhere).

fixes.title: 'Load Previous Setup' closed the dialog and reported a successful restore over a no-op
fixes.summary: Two halves, both in my files. (1) quick_start_checker.dart _handleStartFresh emitted 'Loaded previous setup for M31 from frame 1' on a green success snackbar unconditionally - even when profileId, sequenceId and equipmentSnapshot were all absent and it had restored nothing. It now tracks what was actually re-applied (_applyEquipmentSnapshot returns applied + failures instead of failures alone, so an empty snapshot is no longer indistinguishable from a complete restore), names those items in the snackbar, warns to the log, and shows an amber 'Nothing to load: that session recorded no equipment profile, no sequence and no camera settings.' when nothing was restorable. (2) quick_start_dialog.dart no longer offers the action at all in that state: the primary button renders disabled with the reason underneath, gated on the same three fields the dialog is already reporting as 'Unknown Profile' / 'No Sequence' two rows above.
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/widgets/quick_start_checker_authority_test.dart test/widgets/quick_start_dialog_honesty_test.dart -> 9/9 pass (including the pre-existing 'start fresh warns when saved device positions are skipped', which the applied/failures refactor had to keep working).
fixes.revert_check: Two separate severances. (a) Dialog: restored the original unconditional `else SkotiqButton(... onPressed: onStartFresh)` branch -> 'a session with nothing recorded cannot be loaded' failed. (b) Checker: forced the message selection back to the single `final base = 'Loaded previous setup for $target from frame 1';` -> 'start fresh does not claim a restore it could not perform' failed. Both restored -> all pass.
fixes.caveats: The upstream half is NOT mine and remains open: SessionStateNotifier.startSession still never persists profile_id / sequence_id / equipment_snapshot (blocked item 10, skotiq_core), so on today's builds the honest answer this dialog now gives is 'nothing to load' for most sessions. That is the truth about the recorded data, not a new limitation - and the button no longer lies about it.

fixes.title: The autofocus result overlay never dismissed itself and followed the operator onto every other screen
fixes.summary: COLLISION, resolved in favour of the other agent. I implemented the auto-dismiss in the widget (a 10 s timer armed in AutofocusProgressOverlay.build, skipped for a failed run and for an expanded panel) and had it green and revert-checked. Mid-run the concurrent core-providers agent landed the same fix one layer down, in AutofocusOverlayNotifier (_armResultDismiss / _cancelResultDismiss, resultAutoDismissDelay = 10 s, armed on completed + cancelled, cancelled on start/failure/dismiss/dispose) - which is the better location: it also covers the headless and any non-widget consumer, and it is what the verifier asked for. Two timers racing is a real hazard, so I REVERTED my widget change entirely (autofocus_progress_overlay.dart is now byte-identical to HEAD) and kept only a widget-level regression test, rewritten to assert the user-visible contract through the rendered overlay rather than my implementation: the pill leaves the screen after a completed OR cancelled run, a FAILED run's reason persists, and a new run cancels the previous countdown.
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay_dismiss_test.dart test/widgets/autofocus_progress_overlay_idle_test.dart -> 6/6 pass. The pre-existing idle test matters here: an auto-dismiss timer must not resurrect the never-idles defect, and it does not.
fixes.revert_check: Severed the OTHER agent's production call sites - the two `_armResultDismiss();` lines in onAutofocusCompleted and onAutofocusCancelled - leaving their machinery intact. 'a completed run clears its own summary' and 'a cancelled run also clears itself' both failed. Restored -> 4/4 pass. So these tests do hold the fix down from the UI side regardless of which layer owns the timer.
fixes.caveats: Residual I found while my version was in place, and deliberately did NOT unilaterally add to their file while they were editing it: expanding the pill to study the V-curve does not stop the countdown, so a result the operator opened at t+5 s still vanishes at t+10 s. My widget version cancelled on expand. Worth adding to AutofocusOverlayNotifier (cancel on toggleMinimized -> expanded, re-arm on minimise). Also not done: the verifier's request to route-gate the completed pill to the imaging screen in screens/shell/app_shell.dart - auto-clearing removes the same harm without teaching the shell about routes, and app_shell is outside my ownership.

fixes.title: A chip the operator could not choose rendered identically to one they simply had not chosen
fixes.summary: Design-system gap, found on the Submit-discovery dialog: callers expressed 'disabled' by passing a null onTap to SkotiqChip, and that path rendered exactly the unselected style AND dropped the button role entirely, so a blocked network was neither visibly nor audibly distinguishable from an available one - the panel's explanation of the blocker sat under a control that gave no sign of being blocked. Added an explicit `enabled` flag (default true) that dims fill/border/label, announces Semantics(button: true, enabled: false), and shows the forbidden cursor. `onTap == null && enabled` still means 'status label' and is untouched, because a readout was never an option and must not acquire a button role. Wired the two genuine disabled call sites: transient_report_panel.dart (the AAVSO/MPC/TNS network chips this finding is about) and transients_screen.dart (the MPEC/CBAT source chips, which had been working around the missing affordance by appending '- not available' to the label).
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_ui && flutter test test/skotiq_chip_disabled_test.dart test/design_system_gallery_test.dart test/accessibility_guidelines_test.dart -> 24/24 pass.
fixes.revert_check: Two severances. (a) Full: removed every `!enabled` branch from the component so the flag existed but changed nothing - the render test and the tap test failed. (b) Narrow: removed only the disabled Semantics/MouseRegion branch (restoring `if (onTap == null)`) - the semantics test and the tap test failed. Both restored -> 4/4 pass.
fixes.caveats: The two call-site edits are in screens/ rather than my declared widgets/, but a design-system flag no caller passes is dead code - the item explicitly assigned the shared-widget half to me and the panel half to the (already-finished) r-analytics agent, whose notices this makes legible. WARNING for whoever runs the gates: packages/skotiq_ui/test/golden/design_gallery_golden_test.dart WRITES docs/design/goldens/gallery-*.png rather than comparing, so running it regenerates them on Linux. Those files were already modified in the working tree before I started; my run rewrote them again. Default chips are byte-identical under this change (enabled defaults to true and takes the original code path), so no gallery pixel should have moved - but per the repo rule, do not commit Linux-regenerated goldens.

fixes.title: Every paired device reported 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' while it was actively driving the rig
fixes.summary: paired_devices.last_connected_at had NO writer in production. The only code that stamps it, TokenManager.verifySessionToken, has no production caller (verified by grep): the headless auth middleware authenticates paired bearers against its in-memory _pairedSessionTokens map, which is hydrated FROM Drift at boot and never written back. The middleware now calls _touchPairedDeviceSeen(token) on both authenticated paths - the Authorization-header path and the legacy WS ?token= upgrade - which matches the token to its device row and goes through verifySessionToken, so the stamp is a side effect of the pairing layer's own auditable check (re-tests is_active + expiry in constant time) rather than a bare UPDATE that could mark a device seen on a credential pairing would reject. The write is fire-and-forget (a client request must never block on bookkeeping), throttled to one per token per minute via a new _pairedDeviceSeenStamps map on HeadlessApiServer, bounded against the same ceiling as the token map, and skipped entirely when no PairingService exists so a GUI host never opens Drift just to bookkeep. On failure the throttle entry is dropped so the next request retries.
fixes.test: cd apps/desktop && flutter test test/headless_api_server/ test/headless_api/auth_middleware_test.dart test/headless_api/pairing_handlers_test.dart -> 47/47 pass. The new test boots a real HeadlessApiServer over an in-memory PairingDatabase with a device paired BEFORE start() (the hydration path), issues an authenticated GET /api/status, and asserts lastConnectedAt is stamped within the last minute; a second test asserts an unknown bearer stamps nothing.
fixes.revert_check: Cut both production call sites (`_touchPairedDeviceSeen(token);` after clearFailures in the bearer path, and `_touchPairedDeviceSeen(queryToken);` in the WS ?token= branch), leaving the helper intact. 'an authenticated request records the device as seen' failed (lastConnectedAt still null after the 1 s poll window). Restored -> 2/2 pass.
fixes.caveats: The modern WS path (POST /api/ws/ticket then ?ticket=) cannot be attributed at upgrade time - by design the ticket carries only a SHA-256 identity digest, not the raw token - but minting the ticket is itself an authenticated HTTP request that stamps, so a ticket-based client is still recorded. Cookie-authenticated dashboard sessions are likewise stamped only via their bearer requests. These files are apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/ rather than the literal headless_api/ in my ownership list; I took it as the headless-API owner since no other wave-3 agent touches apps/desktop.

fixes.title: The NIGHT STORY timeline was hidden whenever a session had no science products, even with narrator events recorded
fixes.summary: The Science tab collapses to one shared placeholder when all ten science tables are empty (the audit fix that stopped nine stacked 'no data' cards). That branch dropped the narrator timeline with them, so the operator it exists for - imaged all night, no plate solver, therefore no photometry, no PSF tiles, no calibrations - was exactly the operator whose night narrative, and every detail sheet reachable from it, was suppressed. The NIGHT STORY heading + NightStoryTimeline now render unconditionally in that branch, between the solve-rate card and the ladder, matching their placement in the populated layout. Rendered unconditionally rather than by widening `allEmpty` with narratorFeedProvider: the narrator is a session-narrative surface, not a science product, and the timeline already owns a proper empty state.
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_tab_night_story_test.dart test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_authority_state_test.dart test/screens/analytics/widgets/night_story_timeline_test.dart -> 15/15 pass. The new test pumps the real ScienceAnalyticsTab with a session whose every science provider is empty and one narrator event, and asserts both the heading and the event headline render.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the added block (heading + spacer + NightStoryTimeline) from the allEmpty branch. Both new tests failed. Restored -> both pass.
fixes.caveats: science_analytics_tab.dart is in screens/, not my declared widgets/ - but NightStoryTimeline itself and the narrator card set are packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/narrator/, the item had no owner after r-analytics finished, and the fix is a 6-line composition change in an already-structured branch.

I left it in place rather than delete it - removing another agent's just-landed fix plus its regression tests during a concurrent wave is more risk than the dead code is worth - but it is a real deletion candidate for a quiet moment.
